---
title: "Overview"
subtitle: "How Obsidian, GitHub and gh-inbox fit together, and the daily and weekly loops."
---

Obsidian is where you think and capture. GitHub is the source of truth for task status. `gh-inbox`, a config-driven CLI built on the `gh` CLI, carries information between them: GitHub → Obsidian for what needs you today and what happened this week, Obsidian → GitHub for your efforts and their progress. launchd runs it each weekday morning; an Apple Reminder and two calendar blocks make sure you look at the result.

The same setup works against GitHub Enterprise at work ({{< meta facts.ph.host >}}) and {{< meta facts.ph.home_host >}} at home. Only the [config file](config.qmd) differs.

## How the parts fit

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  L(["launchd<br/>weekday mornings"]) --> D
  N["GitHub<br/>notifications, review requests,<br/>assigned issues"] --> D["gh-inbox"]
  W["GitHub<br/>curious + unsorted repos"] --> G["gh-inbox digest"]
  D --> DN["Obsidian<br/>daily note: inbox block"]
  G --> WN["Obsidian<br/>weekly note: digest block"]
  DN -- "you work the inbox,<br/>write Log bullets" --> S["gh-inbox sync"]
  EF["Obsidian<br/>effort notes: folder = state"] --> S
  S --> R["GitHub<br/>personal repo: one issue per effort"]
  S --> P["GitHub Project<br/>Effort state field"]
  M(["Reminder + Calendar"]) -.-> DN
  M -.-> WN
```

| Part | Role | Page |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub notifications and watching | Decide what reaches you at all | [GitHub settings and notifications](github-settings.qmd) |
| Personal repo and GitHub Project | One issue per effort; board grouped by effort state | [GitHub Project](github-project.qmd) |
| Obsidian vault | Daily and weekly notes, effort notes, Tasks checkboxes | [Obsidian](obsidian.qmd) |
| launchd and the wrapper script | Runs the daily inbox; alerts on failure | [macOS launchd and alerts](launchd.qmd) |
| Apple Reminders and Calendar | Habit nudges to actually do the triage | [Apple Reminders and Calendar](reminders-calendar.qmd) |
| Config file | One file every command reads; the hub everything else lines up with | [gh-inbox config file](config.qmd) |

## Daily loop

{{< include _partials/schedule.qmd >}}

1. **Before you start**, launchd runs `gh-inbox`. It fills the inbox block in today's daily note ({{< meta facts.vault.daily_example >}}) and stamps `updated at`. If it fails, a persistent macOS alert names the log file. See [launchd and alerts](launchd.qmd).
2. **Triage.** The reminder fires and the calendar block starts. Tap the reminder's link to open today's note and work through **{{< meta facts.inbox.waiting >}}**: review, reply, or close. **{{< meta facts.inbox.oldest >}}** is optional. Tick the reminder when {{< meta facts.inbox.waiting >}} is handled; if you don't, it nags again later. Refresh by hand with {{< meta facts.launchd.alias >}}.
3. **During the day**, capture in Obsidian. Tasks stay checkboxes in effort notes; progress goes under {{< meta facts.vault.log_heading >}} in the daily note, one bullet per update, each starting with an effort link. A task that outgrows a checkbox becomes its own effort note.
4. **Sync** with `gh-inbox sync --dry-run`, then `gh-inbox sync`. New `gh`-tagged effort notes become issues, moved notes change state, checkboxes update the issue body, and yesterday's log bullets become issue comments.

Check the heartbeat: if today's inbox block has no `updated at` stamp from today, the job didn't run.

## Weekly loop

1. **{{< meta facts.time.digest_day >}} afternoon**, run `gh-inbox digest`. It writes the digest block into this week's weekly note ({{< meta facts.vault.weekly_example >}}). Re-running the same week refreshes the block; earlier weeks are never touched.
2. **{{< meta facts.time.digest_day >}} {{< meta facts.time.digest >}}**, in the optional {{< meta facts.nudge.digest_block >}} block, read it. Sort anything under {{< meta facts.digest.new_repos >}} into {{< meta facts.tier.core >}} or {{< meta facts.tier.curious >}} in the [config](config.qmd). Skipping a week is fine; old digests age out with their weekly note.
3. **Review efforts.** Look over the [GitHub Project](github-project.qmd) board, then make changes in the vault: move effort notes between state folders as things wake up, stall or finish, and run `gh-inbox sync`. Sync is one way, so a state changed on the board is overwritten by the next sync.
